sections.html: These fish reach the aquariums of interested hobbyists only very seldom. They are specialized surface fish and are only suitable for hobbyists with restrictions because of their rapacious habits.
These needlefish (Belonidae), called halfbeaks, come from almost all over Amazonia. They are also found in the Orinoco catchment area as well as in the Guyana countries.

The fish grow to a maximum of 40 cm and feel best in a small group of 3-6 animals. Aquariums with a base of 150x60 cm are therefore the absolute minimum. The height of the aquarium is not important, as only the first 20 cm and the water surface are used as living space.
They are rather undemanding in further care; you only have to provide an aquarium big enough for these surface predators.

They make heavy demands on the keeper regarding nutrition. In the beginning they mostly react only to living or struggling prey, so you should already have a feeder fish breeding set up, or you can feed them living insects taken from the surface. The animals are particularly excited when crickets, flies or similar insects touch the surface. After settling in, you can try to get the fish used to dead food little by little. Frozen white bloodworms are well-tried, as they float quite long in the water; food that sinks too quickly is not noticed.
Keeping them with other fish is quite possible, but the tank mates should not be prey for them, and should not be so aggressive that they could be dangerous to the peaceful Potamorrhaphis guianensis.
